records.title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. разместил(а) контент: The Pentagon wants a robot boat that launches robot drones. That's not two autonomous systems — it's a much harder problem than boat plus drone. The Department of War and DIU open
records.text: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. разместил(а) контент: The Pentagon wants a robot boat that launches robot drones. That's not two autonomous systems — it's a much harder problem than boat plus drone. The Department of War and DIU opened a solicitation last week (SWAP-USV) for uncrewed surface vessels that carry and launch attack drones — at least two UAS per vessel, one-way and recoverable variants both required, with kinetic strike and battle-damage-assessment capability. It's a direct response to what Ukraine has been doing in the Black Sea: robo-boats launching strike drones from the water, cheaply and repeatably. Total program funding is $100M across three sprints plus $200M in follow-on OT authority, with Sprint 1 alone worth up to $40M. Two things in the actual solicitation text are more interesting than the headlines. First, DIU isn't asking for a boat vendor and a drone vendor separately — it explicitly invites "established maritime manufacturers, autonomy developers, sensor manufacturers, and UAS developers," and says standalone submissions are just as welcome as pre-integrated teams, with the government offering to do the matchmaking itself. Second, whatever gets down-selected has to be genuinely production-ready — prior operational demonstration, an active production line, proven USV/UAS/C2 integration — and in the water for testing within 29 days of down-select. No conceptual designs, no prototype-only entries. Put those two requirements together and you get the real technical challenge: launching and recovering a drone off a moving, pitching platform in sea state, at 10+ knots, with the drone's guidance reacquiring its reference frame the instant it leaves a non-fixed launch point, and comms degradation between the two vehicles failing safe rather than failing open — all of it already proven, not still being figured out. That's why DIU built government-directed matchmaking into the process instead of expecting one prime to own the whole stack: they know most companies hold one piece of this — the launch/recovery mechanism, the handoff protocol, the degraded-comms failsafe logic — and they need those pieces pre-integrated and demonstrated, fast, by whoever ends up on a team. If you're a small company in this space with a proven piece of that seam, the opportunity isn't "wait until you can build the whole system." It's getting that piece demonstrated and integrated — through your own partnership or DIU's matchmaking — before the 29-day clock even starts. https://lnkd.in/gJDeZCcS #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #UAV #USV

records.text: Организация Department of Aerospace Science and Technology - Politecnico di Milano разместила контент: A new milestone for battery safety research at #DAER. 🔋 At the #LaST Laboratory on the Bovisa Candiani Campus, the restored outdoor drop tower has been used for its first test in several decades. A lithium-ion battery module was dropped from a height of 15 metres under controlled conditions to assess its resistance to severe impact loading. The test represents an important step toward the safe integration of battery systems in electric vehicles and aircraft. The activity was carried out within the laboratory for electric vehicle safety, established at LaST with funding from the #PNRR #MOST programme, National Centre for Sustainable Mobility, as part of its Air Mobility activities. The test involved Alessandro Airoldi, Paolo Carlo Astori, Antonio Parcelj, Edoardo Novembre and Antonio Maria Caporale, with the contribution of the #CrashLab and #SIAMS research groups. Find out more: https://lnkd.in/e35S7sHf #Polimi #AerospacePolimi.

records.text: Организация Department of Aerospace Science and Technology - Politecnico di Milano разместила контент: A new paper in Applied Acoustics presents the design and qualification of the anechoic wind tunnel at the Aerodynamics Laboratory of the Department of Aerospace Science and Technology - Politecnico di Milano. Designed and brought into operation in three years within the #MOST Sustainable Mobility National Research Center, the facility supports aeroacoustic research on novel #AdvancedAirMobility configurations and multi-propeller systems. Qualification tests measured flow uniformity within 1.4% and a turbulence intensity of 0.14% at 30 m/s. Acoustic measurements recorded low background-noise levels comparable to state-of-the-art academic facilities, while benchmark tests on a circular cylinder and a #NACA0012 airfoil confirmed the wind tunnel’s suitability for aeronautical aeroacoustics. The new infrastructure fills a major gap in the Italian academic landscape and provides a strategic platform for the national aeroacoustics community. The paper is authored by Gemma Bucherelli, Donato Grassi, Alberto Savino, Alberto Guardone and Alex Zanotti. 🔗 https://lnkd.in/dk2ZuHj8 #Polimi #DAER #AerospacePolimi.

Sachin Jain, Ph.D. разместил(а) контент: The Pentagon wants a robot boat that launches robot drones. That's not two autonomous systems — it's a much harder problem than boat plus drone. The Department of War and DIU opened a solicitation last week (SWAP-USV) for uncrewed surface vessels that carry and launch attack drones — at least two UAS per vessel, one-way and recoverable variants both required, with kinetic strike and battle-damage-assessment capability. It's a direct response to what Ukraine has been doing in the Black Sea: robo-boats launching strike drones from the water, cheaply and repeatably. Total program funding is $100M across three sprints plus $200M in follow-on OT authority, with Sprint 1 alone worth up to $40M. Two things in the actual solicitation text are more interesting than the headlines. First, DIU isn't asking for a boat vendor and a drone vendor separately — it explicitly invites "established maritime manufacturers, autonomy developers, sensor manufacturers, and UAS developers," and says standalone submissions are just as welcome as pre-integrated teams, with the government offering to do the matchmaking itself. Second, whatever gets down-selected has to be genuinely production-ready — prior operational demonstration, an active production line, proven USV/UAS/C2 integration — and in the water for testing within 29 days of down-select. No conceptual designs, no prototype-only entries. Put those two requirements together and you get the real technical challenge: launching and recovering a drone off a moving, pitching platform in sea state, at 10+ knots, with the drone's guidance reacquiring its reference frame the instant it leaves a non-fixed launch point, and comms degradation between the two vehicles failing safe rather than failing open — all of it already proven, not still being figured out. That's why DIU built government-directed matchmaking into the process instead of expecting one prime to own the whole stack: they know most companies hold one piece of this — the launch/recovery mechanism, the handoff protocol, the degraded-comms failsafe logic — and they need those pieces pre-integrated and demonstrated, fast, by whoever ends up on a team. If you're a small company in this space with a proven piece of that seam, the opportunity isn't "wait until you can build the whole system." It's getting that piece demonstrated and integrated — through your own partnership or DIU's matchmaking — before the 29-day clock even starts. https://lnkd.in/gJDeZCcS #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #UAV #USV
